title: Realism, Feminist Critique, and the Security Dilemma

scenes.text: Why does building weapons for self-defense make everyone feel less safe?
scenes.narration: Imagine two neighbors building tall gates for protection, only to terrify each other. Realism says states live in anarchy, meaning there is no global government to protect them.

scenes.text: Distrustful residents install guard dogs, causing panic across the housing society.
scenes.narration: Think of this analogy like a housing society without security guards. When a neighbor buys a guard dog to feel safe, you panic and buy one too. Soon, everyone is armed and terrified.

scenes.name: Hans Morgenthau
scenes.idea: International politics is a struggle for power driven by human nature.
scenes.narration: Hans Morgenthau, the father of realism, published Politics Among Nations in nineteen forty-nine. He argued that states naturally seek power to survive, making national interest their supreme motivation.

scenes.heading: Morgenthau versus Tickner
scenes.narration: Feminist scholar Ann Tickner challenged Morgenthau's masculine worldview. She explained that power means collective empowerment and human security, not just domination.

scenes.heading: Herz's Security Dilemma Cycle
scenes.narration: John Herz called this cycle the security dilemma. Because states lack trust, one nation arming for defense makes neighbors feel insecure and buy weapons too, spiraling toward war.

scenes.heading: Jervis's Security Dilemma Scenarios
cells: Intense dilemma but lower arms race
scenes.narration: Robert Jervis showed that this dilemma depends on technology and geography. It is doubly dangerous when offensive and defensive weapons look identical, and attacking gives an advantage.

scenes.heading: Third World Insecurity Dilemma
items: Security dilemma is a Eurocentric concept
Developing states face internal civil wars
Internal insecurity matters more than invasions
scenes.narration: Scholars Amitav Acharya and Mohammad Ayoob argue this dilemma is Eurocentric. Developing nations face an insecurity dilemma, where internal threats like civil wars matter far more than foreign invasions.

items: Morgenthau views politics as power struggles under anarchy
Tickner redefines power toward human security and ethics
Security and insecurity dilemmas explain mutual fear
scenes.narration: Here is the trick to remember. Realism explains power struggles under anarchy, feminism demands human security and ethics, while security dilemmas show how mutual fear sparks conflict.
